messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty: HIGH — gpu-serving-cluster/cuda_alloc_failures fired for service=redwood-inference-gen4 (46 events in 5m). Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD12345
PagerDutyBot: Notification sent to escalation policy 'eng-oncall'
Alex M: acked the pager — I'll start triage. Seeing surge in cudaAlloc failures from the gen4 pool.
Samir: +1 seeing the same in traces.  tail latency spikes and a bunch of 5xx from model-proxy containers.
Priya K: any obvious node-level OOMs?
Samir: grabbing nvidia-smi and dmesg now
Samir: ```
# nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
GPU 0
    FB Memory Usage
        Total                       : 32536 MiB
        Used                        : 32330 MiB
        Free                        : 206 MiB

# dmesg | tail -n 40
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65): 79, pid=28765, GPU has failed to allocate memory
[ 1234.568100] cuda: alloc failed: out of memory
```
Priya K: Xid 79 usually indicates out-of-memory allocation failures in the driver stack, sometimes fragmentation.
Alex M: Are these concentrated to particular nodes or pods?
Samir: Mostly node-gen4-7 and node-gen4-9. Both show repeated kernel warnings and kvcache evictions.
Samir: ```
# kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gen4-7
model-proxy-xyz  2/2  Running  1  3m  node-gen4-7
inference-worker-abc  1/1  Running  0  6m  node-gen4-7
```
Samir: Logs from model-proxy show `cudaMalloc` retries and `Allocation failed: 0xC0000010` before it falls back to CPU and sometimes crashes.
Priya K: Impact on customers? Any 504/timeout spikes?
Alex M: Alerting shows ~3% of requests in region-us-west are hitting 5xx within the last 10m. One large customer (acme-inc) reported degraded responses.
Alex M: I'll open a quick incident summary for support.
Alex M: Mitigation plan options: 1) Evict pods on affected nodes to force scheduling to healthy nodes 2) Restart kubelet on nodes to clear driver state 3) Trigger autoscale to spin up extra gen4 nodes 4) Force fallback to CPU pools for low-priority routes while we stabilize.
Samir: Evicting pods + node restart seems fastest. We'll lose warm KV cache but should recover.
Priya K: Before restarting, drain node-gen4-7 -> cordon -> drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then rotate.
Alex M: I'm doing cordon+drain on node-gen4-7 now. Command: `kubectl cordon node-gen4-7 && kubectl drain node-gen4-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
IncidentBot: Action recorded: node-gen4-7 cordoned by Alex M
Samir: After drain, watching scheduler pack to node-gen4-2 and gen4-11 which have more free FB memory.
Samir: nvidia-smi on gen4-7 post-evict shows GPU memory back at 120MiB used. Good.
Priya K: I'm going to restart nvidia driver on gen4-9 with `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` and then `modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia` if needed. Coordinating now.
Alex M: Update: cordon+drain completed for gen4-7, some traffic rerouted. error rate dropped to ~1.2% in last 5m.
Samir: gen4-9 driver restart in progress... got transient node kernel warning during unload, driver came back up. Monitoring.
Priya K: After restart, requesting to bump autoshedder thresholds to aggressively evict large-batch sessions for 30m to reduce memory pressure: `POST /admin/autoshedder?mode=aggressive&ttl=1800` (performed).
Alex M: Noted. Also enabling CPU-fallback for low-priority keys: `route-config set --route lowpri --fallback cpu` — applying now.
IncidentBot: Change applied by Alex M: fallback enabled for route lowpri
Samir: Observing fewer cudaAlloc failures after both restarts and autoshedder tweak. Xid 79 errors decreased from 7/min to ~1/min.
Alex M: Customer impact: support ticket opened for acme-inc (INC-9073), noted degraded response window 2026-03-14T03:45Z -> ongoing; currently partial impact, mitigation in progress.
Priya K: We'll keep node-gen4-9 unscheduled for another hour to ensure driver stability, and run a post-mortem check for fragmentation (collect `cuda-memcheck`, driver logs).
Alex M: Handoff to next on-call in 20m: @oncall-next — please monitor Xid spikes and ensure autoshedder TTL is reverted after 30m. If failures persist, escalate to infra and consider scheduling a rolling kernel/driver update.
oncall-next: acknowledged, I'll take over at 04:10Z. Steps I'll follow: 1) verify Xid rate; 2) check pod crashloop trends; 3) coordinate node reboots if Xid rate >3/min for >10m; 4) notify Support if any large customers still affected.
Alex M: adding runbook links: https://redwood.example/runbooks/gpu-xid-and-oom and postmortem template.
Priya K: Quick notes for followup: collect `dmesg`, `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log`, `nvidia-smi -q`, kernel oops dumps, and kvcache size histograms for the last 6h. Attach to incident doc.
Samir: I'll schedule a follow-up meeting tomorrow to look at model batch sizing and quantization options that might reduce FB usage.
Alex M: Thanks all. Keeping the thread open until oncall-next confirms stable.
oncall-next: confirming stable at 04:25Z — Xid back to baseline, error rate ~0.2%. I'll close after 30m of stability.
IncidentBot: Incident marked stable by oncall-next
PagerDutyBot: Incident resolved auto-close scheduled in 1h unless reopened.
Alex M: Filed follow-up ticket INF-2291 for driver fragmentation investigation and potential driver/firmware update plan.
Priya K: nice work team :thumbsup:
